---
title: "Glossary"
toc-depth: 2
---

Use these definitions to distinguish observations, assessment, access and delivery. They follow
MISP **3.0.0**, `3.0_wip` commit `99ebee729`; an integration's terminology or an older API
specification may use the same word differently. Links lead to the detailed procedures.

<!-- Source and validation provenance: assets/appendices-screenshots.json -->

## A–C {#glossary-a-c}

<a id="analyst-data"></a>

### Analyst Data {#glossary-analyst-data}

Research records associated with supported MISP targets: **Notes** hold commentary,
**Opinions** express an assessment, and **Relationships** state typed links. They retain their
own authorship/ownership and visibility rather than rewriting the observed fact. MISP 3.0 also
supports value-targeted research. Sharing an event does not automatically make every associated
research record visible. See [Analyst Data](analyst-data/index.qmd#the-three-types).

<a id="api"></a>

### API {#glossary-api}

An application programming interface: the operations, inputs and responses through which a
client interacts with MISP. REST endpoints support automation, lookup and sharing; permission,
record-visibility and key restrictions still apply. PyMISP is a Python client for that API, not
a second MISP server. See [Automation & API](automation/index.qmd#api-reference).

Earlier terminology adapted from Wikipedia's [API](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_programming_interface)
entry, [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/).

### API key {#glossary-api-key}

A credential associated with a MISP user. Its expiry, allowed IPs, read-only restrictions and
other supported controls supplement the account's permissions. It is distinct from a browser
password, a CustomAuth external key and a remote peer's configuration. See
[authentication keys](administration/index.qmd#admin-authentication).

### Cache {#glossary-cache}

A stored representation used to accelerate lookup or avoid repeating a fetch. Feed/remote-data
caches are distinct from fully imported local events, and job Redis storage is another use of
Redis again. Cache presence does not prove freshness, local ownership or permission to share.
See [feed management](managing-feeds/index.qmd#feeds).

<a id="cerebrate"></a>

### Cerebrate {#glossary-cerebrate}

A companion platform for managing community and organisation information. MISP can use a
configured connection to obtain supported organisation/sharing-group definitions. The integration
has its own credentials and update process; it does not replace event distribution or the need
to verify identities. See [connectors](connectors/index.qmd#connectors-mechanisms).

<a id="collection"></a>

### Collection {#glossary-collection}

A curated resource that references supported elements such as events and galaxy clusters.
Its own access and sharing settings do not flatten the members' visibility or ensure that every
recipient receives every referenced item. See [Collections](collections/index.qmd#what-a-collection-contains).

<a id="community"></a>

### Community {#glossary-community}

People and organisations that cooperate on intelligence sharing under agreed practices and
trust relationships. An instance, organisation, sharing group and synchronization link are
technical structures used by a community; none alone describes its entire governance or membership.

### Correlation {#glossary-correlation}

A link discovered between relevant matching observations according to the configured engine,
types, exclusions and visibility. It is a pivot for investigation, not proof of common ownership,
maliciousness, causality or attribution. See
[value and correlation maintenance](administration/index.qmd#admin-correlations).

## D–I {#glossary-d-i}

<a id="decaying-model"></a>

### Decaying Model {#glossary-decaying-model}

A configurable way to score an indicator's remaining relevance over time using the supported
inputs and parameters. A score informs selection/review; it does not inherently delete the
observation, clear IDS or deploy a downstream response. See
[decaying models](decaying-models/index.qmd#how-scoring-works).

### Distribution {#glossary-distribution}

The audience/sharing scope of a supported record. Event, child-record, analyst-data and knowledge
scopes have their own rules; tags and publication do not override them. Child inheritance uses
stored value **5**, while sharing-group distribution needs an actual group. See
[distribution boundaries](sharing/index.qmd#distribution-mechanisms).

<a id="event-report"></a>

### Event Report {#glossary-event-report}

A Markdown report attached to an event, used to explain observations, sources and analysis.
MISP element references connect the narrative to the underlying records. Extraction/import and
export capabilities depend on the supported action and deployment; a report is not automatically
an independent case-management record. See [Event Reports](event-reports/index.qmd#writing-a-report).

### IDS flag {#glossary-ids-flag}

The attribute's `to_ids` flag, indicating intended use in supported detection-oriented exports
or selection. It is separate from correlation, distribution and an assessment of maliciousness.
An attribute with IDS off remains a usable observation; IDS on does not install a detection rule
in another tool. See [attribute fields](categories-and-types/index.qmd#attribute-categories-vs-types).

<a id="indicators"></a>

### Indicators {#glossary-indicators}

Patterns or observations selected for a detection or intelligence purpose with enough context
to explain their intended use. A string extracted from a report, a warninglist miss or an IDS
default does not by itself establish a useful indicator. See
[detection exports](user-stories/index.qmd#stories-detection).

<a id="ioc"></a>

### IOC {#glossary-ioc}

An **indicator of compromise**: an artefact or pattern that may support identifying intrusion
or compromise in context. A domain, hash or address is an observation before its significance
has been assessed; the term does not make every occurrence malicious.

## J–M {#glossary-j-m}

### Job {#glossary-job}

A unit of work and its execution/status record. A SQL job ID and the backend process/job UUID
are different identifiers. Waiting, running, successful and failed states require inspection of
the actual outcome. See [background jobs](administration/index.qmd#admin-background-jobs).

<a id="local-tags"></a>

### Local tags {#glossary-local-tags}

Instance-local **attachments** of tags or galaxy context to supported targets. They allow
local classification without asserting a shared change to the owner's observation. Normal
native synchronization excludes local attachments; check manual/format-specific exports
separately. A tag definition and one attachment's local/global scope are distinct. See
[taxonomy scope](taxonomy/index.qmd#taxonomy-use).

<a id="malware-information-sharing-platform-and-threat-sharing"></a>

<a id="misp"></a>

### MISP {#glossary-misp}

The **MISP Intelligence Sharing Platform**, commonly called MISP. The project's historical
name referred to malware information sharing; its present scope includes broader threat
intelligence, observations, knowledge and collaborative analysis. The acronym is also used
recursively as “MISP Intelligence Sharing Platform”.

<a id="misp-attribute"></a>

### MISP Attribute {#glossary-misp-attribute}

One typed occurrence of a value in an investigative context, with its own UUID, category,
observation times, flags and access context. It may stand alone in an event or be an object
relation. In 3.0, its component values also have shared addresses, which do not replace that
occurrence identity. See [categories and types](categories-and-types/index.qmd#types-values).

<a id="misp-event"></a>

### MISP Event {#glossary-misp-event}

A container for contextually related observations, objects, reports and other supported records,
with a creator/owner context, distribution and publication state. It is not necessarily one
confirmed real-world incident. See [creating an event](using-the-system/index.qmd#creating-an-event).

<a id="misp-extended-events"></a>

### MISP Extended Events {#glossary-misp-extended-events}

Separately owned events linked to an original event to contribute additional observations.
A combined view remains subject to visibility; extension does not transfer ownership of all
the original data. See [extended events](extended-events/index.qmd#when-to-use-an-extended-event).

<a id="misp-feeds"></a>

### MISP feeds {#glossary-misp-feeds}

Sources that MISP can cache, compare or import using a supported format/configuration.
Caching context and importing full events have different storage and update behaviour. Review
the source's terms, identifiers, format and quality before enabling it. See
[feed management](managing-feeds/index.qmd#feeds).

<a id="misp-format"></a>

### MISP format {#glossary-misp-format}

The native data structures and interchange contracts used for MISP records. Consult the
[MISP format specifications](https://github.com/MISP/misp-rfc) together with the installed
implementation and client version. MISP JSON, a STIX export and an arbitrary API response are
not interchangeable contracts. See [API reference](automation/index.qmd#api-reference).

<a id="misp-galaxy-cluster"></a>

### MISP Galaxy Cluster {#glossary-misp-galaxy-cluster}

An identifiable knowledge entry within a galaxy, with a UUID, description, metadata, version
and supported relationships. An attachment connects that context to an observation using a tag
and local/global scope. Shipped and custom tag representations can differ; read the stored
identity rather than constructing it from a display label. See
[galaxies](galaxy/index.qmd#galaxy-concepts).

<a id="misp-gnupg-key"></a>

### MISP GnuPG Key {#glossary-misp-gnupg-key}

The instance's configured OpenPGP key used by supported notification-signing/encryption workflows.
Manage it according to the mail deployment's identity, protection and lifecycle requirements.
It is separate from an event-signing key in the protected-event system. See
[mail settings](administration/index.qmd#admin-configuration-baseline).

<a id="misp-instance"></a>

### MISP Instance {#glossary-misp-instance}

A deployment of the MISP application, its datastores and configured services. Local versus
remote describes the instance from which a request or sharing operation is being considered;
a connected instance is not automatically entitled to every local record. Files/object storage,
caches and external providers also matter when operating or backing up the service.

<a id="misp-modules"></a>

### MISP modules {#glossary-misp-modules}

A companion service providing supported enrichment, import, export or other module operations.
The service, module dependencies, configuration and provider access must be present for a
particular action to work. A module result is a sourced claim requiring interpretation, and a
live lookup can disclose submitted data to a provider. See [Modules](modules/index.qmd#modules-families).

<a id="misp-noticelist"></a>

### MISP noticelist {#glossary-misp-noticelist}

A definition that supplies informational guidance on supported entry forms. In the pinned
implementation, attribute-form checks use category/type triggers. It is not an arbitrary
value-matching engine, an automatic access policy or proof of compliance. See
[notice lists](noticelists/index.qmd#noticelists-triggers).

<a id="misp-objects"></a>

### MISP Objects {#glossary-misp-objects}

Structured observations composed of attributes with named object relations, based on an
object template. Each instance/attribute retains its own identity and context. Template
requirements can allow a single-attribute object; object references declare directional links
to observed entities. See [MISP objects](misp-objects/index.qmd#objects-use).

<a id="misp-sightings"></a>

### MISP Sightings {#glossary-misp-sightings}

Records associated with an observed value/attribute context, such as a positive observation,
false-positive claim or expiration claim, with source/time information as supported. They
inform assessment; they do not automatically validate a threat or change every IDS flag.
See [Sightings](sightings/index.qmd#explanation).

<a id="misp-taxonomies"></a>

### MISP Taxonomies {#glossary-misp-taxonomies}

Controlled classification vocabularies expressed through machine tags: a namespace and
predicate, optionally with a value. Their handling/classification meanings are separate from
an access grant. Enable the intended vocabulary and tags, then choose the attachment scope.
See [Taxonomies](taxonomy/index.qmd#taxonomy-machine-tags).

Earlier terminology adapted from Wikipedia's
[Taxonomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomy_(general)) entry,
[CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/).

<a id="misp-warninglists"></a>

### MISP warninglists {#glossary-misp-warninglists}

Lists whose enabled matching rules identify values that merit contextual review: for example,
known infrastructure or potential false positives. A hit is not a universal benign/malicious
verdict. Warning display and export filtering can have different scopes. See
[Warning Lists](warninglists/index.qmd#warninglists-use).

## N–O {#glossary-n-o}

<a id="nids"></a>

### NIDS {#glossary-nids}

A **network intrusion detection system**, such as a compatible Snort/Suricata deployment.
A MISP export must fit that system's format and operational policy; generating a ruleset does
not establish that it was deployed or is effective.

### Object template {#glossary-object-template}

A definition of relation names, attribute types, constraints and presentation for an observed
object. Its UUID/version identify the template, not a particular observation. Updating the
catalogue does not silently migrate every saved instance. See
[object templates](misp-objects/index.qmd#objects-maintenance).

<a id="observable"></a>

### Observable {#glossary-observable}

Something observed, such as a file, address or activity, represented with the data model and
context appropriate to the source. Other standards use the term in their own schemas. It is
not an exact synonym for “MISP attribute with IDS off”; observations can be represented by
several attributes or an object, and detection use is a separate decision.

### Occurrence {#glossary-occurrence}

One attribute record in its event/object context, identified by its attribute UUID. Several
occurrences can share component values while retaining different sources, times, roles,
ownership and visibility. See [3.0 values](categories-and-types/index.qmd#types-values).

<a id="org-admin"></a>

### Org Admin {#glossary-org-admin}

An **organisation administrator**, with the account-management scope granted by the role and
applicable organisation checks. This is distinct from site administration. The title does not
grant global role editing, server configuration or unrestricted access to other organisations.
See [administrative access](administration/index.qmd#admin-access).

### Organisation {#glossary-organisation}

A local or known remote organisational identity, with a UUID used in sharing relationships.
Local database IDs are instance-specific. Creator/owner identity, membership in an organisation
and membership of a sharing group answer different questions. See
[organisation identities](administration/index.qmd#organisations).

<a id="osint"></a>

### OSINT {#glossary-osint}

**Open-source intelligence**: information collected from publicly available sources and used
in an intelligence context. “Open” describes source availability, not open-source software,
redistribution rights or verified accuracy.

Earlier terminology adapted from Wikipedia's
[Open-source intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_intelligence) entry,
[CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/).

## P–R {#glossary-p-r}

<a id="pivot-path"></a>

### Pivot path {#glossary-pivot-path}

A sequence of links followed during an investigation, such as accessible occurrences,
correlations or declared relationships. A path records navigable context, not a chain of proof.

<a id="pivoting"></a>

### Pivoting {#glossary-pivoting}

Moving from a starting observation to relevant accessible context. In 3.0 this can include
value views, workspaces, graphs and knowledge entries as well as event-to-event correlation.
See [investigation workflows](user-stories/index.qmd#stories-investigate).

<a id="proposals"></a>

### Proposals {#glossary-proposals}

Suggested attribute additions or changes for an owner/reviewer to assess through the supported
proposal workflow. Acceptance changes the relevant data and requires the appropriate rights.
An attribute proposal is distinct from a separately owned extended event or a complete
object-template proposal. See [the proposal FAQ](faq/index.qmd#faq-object-proposals).

### Protected event {#glossary-protected-event}

An event using the supported cryptographic signing/protection mechanism. Verification concerns
the signed material and the trusted signing identity; it does not prove the truth of every
assessment or widen distribution. See [cryptographic keys](cryptographic-keys/index.qmd#how-it-works).

<a id="publishing"></a>

### Publishing {#glossary-publishing}

A deliberate event release/state transition performed with the relevant permissions and checks.
It makes an eligible event available to supported sharing/notification processes; it does not
make private data public or bypass distribution. Unpublished data can still be visible locally
and accessible to an authorized API/export selection. Mail and peer delivery depend on their
configuration and results. See [publication](using-the-system/index.qmd#publish-an-event).

<a id="pull"></a>

### Pull {#glossary-pull}

Retrieving eligible data from a configured remote instance using the relevant credentials,
rules and update/checkpoint behaviour. It is not a guarantee of downloading every record the
remote instance stores. See [push and pull](sharing/index.qmd#pull-vs-push-synchronisation).

<a id="push"></a>

### Push {#glossary-push}

Sending eligible data to a configured remote instance, subject to identities, publication,
distribution, filters and the recipient's accepted contract. A successful connection test does
not establish that a particular record was delivered. See
[synchronization checks](sharing/index.qmd#troubleshooting).

<a id="restful"></a>

### RESTful {#glossary-restful}

An interface style based on representations of resources and HTTP operations. In MISP,
endpoint-specific routes, parameters and response shapes remain part of the actual contract;
calling a service “RESTful” does not make every action or format interchangeable.
See [API reference](automation/index.qmd#api-reference).

Earlier terminology adapted from Wikipedia's
[Representational state transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer)
entry, [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/).

<a id="roles"></a>

### Roles {#glossary-roles}

Local permission definitions assigned to users. They control capabilities alongside access
levels, dynamic checks and resource limits; record-level visibility and ownership still matter.
Role IDs are local database identifiers, not universal labels for privileges. See
[roles](administration/index.qmd#roles) and
[ACL descriptors](appendices/index.qmd#appendix-b-acl-descriptors).

## S–T {#glossary-s-t}

<a id="scheduled-tasks"></a>

### Scheduled Tasks {#glossary-scheduled-tasks}

Configured recurring operations with an interval, next execution, action and execution user.
The 3.0 task scheduler discovers due tasks and queues work; a saved schedule is distinct from
a running scheduler or a successful job. See
[recurring tasks](administration/index.qmd#admin-scheduled-tasks).

<a id="sharing-groups"></a>

### Sharing groups {#glossary-sharing-groups}

Reusable distribution scopes combining the intended organisation and server memberships with
their sharing rules. They can include local and remote organisations, and must account for
relay/hosting trust. A group is not an end-to-end secrecy channel through an excluded host.
See [sharing groups](sharing/index.qmd#sharing-groups).

<a id="site-admin"></a>

### Site admin {#glossary-site-admin}

A user whose role grants site administration for instance-wide operations, such as global
settings and role/account management. Treat this as privileged access, separate from ordinary
organisation administration; resource-specific/dynamic checks can still apply. See
[administrative access](administration/index.qmd#admin-access).

<a id="standard-misp-install"></a>

### Standard MISP Install {#glossary-standard-misp-install}

An installation following the supported process for its chosen deployment/release. Filesystem,
container and orchestrated deployments can have different paths and service identities; the
phrase does not imply a universal `/var/www/MISP` layout or dependency set. See
[deployment choices](get-your-instance/index.qmd#choosing-a-deployment-method).

<a id="sync-user"></a>

### Sync User {#glossary-sync-user}

An account used by a peer connection with the required API/synchronization permissions and
intended organisation identity. Its key and applicable account state must allow the requested
operation. Connection, owner identity and sharing rules still need verification. See
[sync identities](sharing/index.qmd#concept).

<a id="synchronisation"></a>

### Synchronisation {#glossary-synchronisation}

The exchange of supported data and updates between instances through configured push/pull
mechanisms. Native MISP synchronization, feed import and TAXII integration have different
contracts and scopes. See [sharing options](sharing/index.qmd#sharing-overview).

<a id="tagging"></a>

### Tagging {#glossary-tagging}

Attaching classification/context labels to supported records with the appropriate permission
and local/global scope. A tag can be used in a filter or configured automation policy; its
presence alone does not trigger every action, change IDS or grant access. See
[taxonomy use](taxonomy/index.qmd#taxonomy-use).

<a id="templating"></a>

### Templating {#glossary-templating}

Using definitions/forms to guide structured entry. Object templates describe relations and
constraints; event-entry templates/forms are a different mechanism. A template is separate
from the observed instance created with it. See
[object authoring](misp-objects/index.qmd#objects-authoring).

## V–W {#glossary-v-w}

### Value {#glossary-value}

A stored component value used across attribute occurrences in MISP 3.0. A composite attribute
can have separate component values. Equal stored values do not merge occurrences or establish
their interpretation, ownership or visibility. See
[value identities](categories-and-types/index.qmd#types-values).

### Value address {#glossary-value-address}

The SHA-256 address MISP assigns to a stored normalized component value. Use the returned
address rather than hashing an unnormalized input. It is distinct from a file-hash attribute,
an occurrence UUID, an event UUID and an access grant. See
[value APIs](automation/index.qmd#api-value-targets).

### Worker {#glossary-worker}

A managed process consuming the intended background-job queue. In 3.0, ordinary queue workers
use `start_worker`; the recurring-task poller uses `scheduler_worker`. Supervisor process state,
Redis reachability and job completion are distinct checks. See
[background processing](appendices/index.qmd#appendix-jobs-workers).

<a id="workflow"></a>

### Workflow {#glossary-workflow}

An automation graph connecting supported triggers, conditions and actions. Blocking and
non-blocking execution paths differ; a graph/blueprint alone does not enable every trigger or
provider. Workflows are distinct from recurring task schedules. See
[Workflows](workflows/index.qmd#workflow-hub).

### Workspace {#glossary-workspace}

A 3.0 research context for organizing and exploring supported graph elements and relationships.
Its saved state and visibility are separate from ownership/distribution of the underlying
records. A layout or edge is an investigative aid rather than evidence of causality. See
[investigation workflows](user-stories/index.qmd#stories-investigate).

## Maintaining this glossary {#glossary-maintenance}

Use a concise definition and a link to the relevant procedure. Distinguish terminology from
specific deployments, avoid claiming automatic enforcement without a configured mechanism,
and retain source/licence attribution for adapted material. A broad term does not prevent
adding a more specific term in this Quarto glossary.
